page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.16-64 is a compute instance powered by the 64-bit Arm Ampere AmpereOne processor running at a base clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated physical cores representing 32 vCPUs, utilizing a single thread per core topology. This dedicated hardware profile eliminates resource contention often introduced by simultaneous multithreading. System memory is sized at 64.0 GB, which yields an allocation of 2.0 GB per physical core.

Hardware provisions do not include integrated local disk storage, requiring persistence to be managed through network-attached block volumes. There are no discrete GPU accelerators attached to this instance profile. For network connectivity, the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. In qualitative terms, the AmpereOne architecture emphasizes high core count density and execution efficiency, providing an economical compute-to-core ratio for scalable workloads that do not demand large per-core memory footprints.

Because the platform relies on the arm64 instruction set, workloads compiled specifically for x86 architectures without AArch64 support are not compatible. The 1:2 core-to-memory ratio makes this server suitable for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, containerized microservices, continuous integration runners, high-concurrency web serving, and distributed computational tasks.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.16-64 is an arm64 compute-focused instance powered by the Ampere AmpereOne processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The configuration supplies 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, providing deterministic processing performance across all cores. It includes 64.0 GB of total system RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per core memory footprint. The instance includes no bundled local storage, necessitating remote block storage for persistent filesystems, and features zero dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. With its high core density and efficient Arm architecture, the instance provides qualitative cost-to-core advantages for parallelized computing. VM.Standard.A2.Flex.16-64 is appropriate for multi-threaded build environments, containerized microservices, high-concurrency web serving, and general-purpose parallel tasks optimized for 64-bit Arm architectures.
